decisions.statement: A tick takes away the pages the census judges stale and no others.
No page judged working or undetermined is taken away by a tick.
A tick judges through the same command a person runs by hand.
A tick sweeps the main checkout rather than the tree the service runs from.
A tick that finds nothing stale writes nothing and takes no lock.
A tick says which pages went and says nothing where none went.
A page taken away goes as a commit, so what it was stays in history.
A subagent dispatched again takes its page back out of that history.
A landing another landing holds the lock against writes nothing and says so.
A tick that wrote nothing for a held lock ran rather than failed.
A tick that cannot run at all carries its fault out and fails the unit.
A tick costs 5 to 19 seconds of processor and peaks between 1 and 2 GB.
A tick waits up to 300 seconds for the landing lock every seat shares.
A tick is allowed longer than that wait, so a held lock ends a tick gently.
systemd runs one tick of a unit at a time, whatever the timer does meanwhile.
A timer elapsing during a tick joins that tick rather than starting a second one.
An interval under a tick's own ceiling is therefore safe and costs a skipped tick.
Reading which pages carry a stop costs a quarter second and 135 MB over 24 pages.
That reading is the whole of a tick's work where no page carries a stop.
That cheap reading shares this clock with the full census rather than running oftener.
A tick reads the tree and then waits, so waiting longer means more moved under it.
A tick whose paths moved while it waited writes nothing and names what moved.
That tick ran rather than failed, and the tick after it reads the tree again.
A tick keeps no edits, so a tick leaves nothing behind for the next tick.
A page gone between the census and the take leaves the take saying so.
How often a tick runs bounds how long a stopped subagent's row stays up.
No page's age is read to decide what goes.

definition: the service taking away every subagent page the census judges stale
